cl_coc_nose_damage.q: What does snorting coke do to your nose, and does it heal?
cl_coc_nose_damage.short: It can make a hole in the wall between your nostrils, and damage can spread. 126 of 127 people with this damage had that hole. Healing after stopping hasn't been studied.
cl_coc_nose_damage.but: These are people who already had damage and went to doctors. Nobody knows how many people who snort get it.
how: 17 published case series held 127 people with this damage. 126 had a hole in the septum, the wall between the nostrils. Fewer had damage further in: about 59 in 100 on the lower side walls, 30 in 100 in the roof of the mouth, 23 in 100 higher up, 8 in 100 at the eye socket or skull base.

It can look like a disease that inflames blood vessels. In one Italian clinic, a blood test for that disease was positive in 13 of 18 people with cocaine damage, and some were first treated for that disease, which didn't help. Unlike many with that disease, none of the 18 had fever or illness elsewhere in the body.

None of these studies followed people after they stopped. In the Italian clinic, 4 people were scanned again months or years later. All 4 had kept using cocaine, and all had more damage. In one, it reached the base of the skull within three years.

18 nose doctors agreed, as opinion, that stopping is the only known way to halt the damage. They said no amount of use is safe for it. They'd wait for drug tests showing 12 months off cocaine before repair surgery.
cl_coc_nose_damage.rate: Reports of people who already had damage, often picked for one kind of problem, with no count of how many people who snort get it. Healing after stopping hasn't been studied; what experts say about it is opinion.

cocaine.statement: Studies show a hole in the nose from snorting closes up once you stop.
cocaine.why: None of these studies followed people after they stopped. Experts think stopping is the only known way to halt the damage, but that's opinion.

cocaine.statement: Snorting cocaine can damage the roof of your mouth, not just your nose.
cocaine.why: In 17 published case series, about 30 in 100 people with this damage had it in the roof of the mouth. Nobody knows how many people who snort get it.
